'429':
          description: |
            The file may not have been stored. Phones don't retry on 429, and nothing is lost:
            app.log carries its lines into the next upload, and the other files are full copies
            every time. One of:

            - KEY_EXISTS: another file of this type from this phone was stored in the same
              millisecond. Nothing is overwritten, and the next upload gets a new receive time
              (ADR 0011).
            - STORAGE_FAILED: S3 failed the write or it ran past its 60 s deadline. Once the whole
              body was sent, S3 can still commit the object after the deadline. Never 503.
    head:
      summary: Always 404
      description: Each upload stands alone, so there is never a stored file to compare against.
      operationId: headLog

content.text:
When the S3 write fails or runs past its deadline, the upload service returns **429 Too Many Requests**, with the rejection reason `STORAGE_FAILED`. The deadline is 60 s. The file may still have been stored, because once the whole body was sent, S3 can still commit the object after the deadline. Phones don't retry on 429, and nothing is lost: `app.log` carries its lines into the next upload, and the other files are full copies every time.

It must **never return 503**. This is a hard rule from ADR 0009 and the root CLAUDE.md, and `OpenApiDocumentTest` checks that the API spec lists no 503 response.
